commits.subject: Stop an Infinity phase duration wedging the chart in a rAF loop

original.subject: Fix ANIM-1: Infinity phase duration wedges the chart in a permanent rAF loop
original.body:
An explicit value-axis `min` above the data (or `max` below it) inverts the
domain, so its extent goes negative. `getPositiveDomainDeltaPercentage`
weights a phase as `deltaExtent / (deltaExtent + domainExtent)`, and a growth
delta of the same magnitude cancelled that denominator to exactly zero:

  valueAxes: [{ min: 0 }] with all-negative data -> domain [0, -5], extent -5
  values grow -5 -> 0                            -> delta [0, 5]
  5 / (5 + -5) = Infinity                        -> 400ms * Infinity

`MochartTween.update` then computes `(time - startTime) / Infinity`, which is
0 forever, so the tween never reaches 1, `completeCallback` never fires and
the requestAnimationFrame loop never terminates. The chart freezes on the
first expansion frame. `min: 0` to pin bars at zero on a series that later
goes negative is an ordinary configuration.

Clamp the denominator with `Math.max(domainExtent, 0)`. That alone is
sufficient and total: inside that branch `domainDeltaExtent` is strictly
positive, so the denominator is >= the numerator and the ratio lands in
(0, 1] — no separate result clamp is needed.

Add `safeDuration()` as a second line of defence, mapping any non-finite or
negative duration to 0 (instant) rather than letting it reach the tween. It
covers all four phase durations: the three in `buildDataTween` and the focus
tween, which derives its duration the same way from a delta percentage.

Regression test drives real frames on a fake clock and asserts the animation
settles with no pending frame request; it fails on the unpatched source. Note
the finding's claim that `max: 0` with all-positive data "hangs identically"
does not reproduce — only the `min` case does. The `max` case is kept as a
second test anyway.

The finding's separate `min < max` validation suggestion is left open as a
question in REVIEW-FINDINGS-NEW.md: with `strict` defaulting to true a warning
invalidates a config exactly as an error does, so it is a behavioural choice
rather than an obvious fix.

commits.subject: Stop null data collapsing the value axis to a single point

original.subject: Fix DATA-1: null in the data collapses the value axis to a single point
original.body:
The missing-value guard in `getDomainForValues` was
`value !== undefined && !Number.isNaN(value)`. `Number.isNaN(null)` is false,
so null reached the comparisons — where `min === null` doubles as the "no
minimum yet" sentinel. `null < min` is true for any positive min (null
coerces to 0), so assigning `min = null` re-armed the sentinel and discarded
every minimum seen so far:

  getDomainForValues([5, null, 20])  -> [20, 20]   every point on one pixel
  getDomainForValues([10, null])     -> [null, 10] breaks the null-pair invariant
  getDomainForValues([10, Infinity]) -> [10, null]

null is the standard JSON/API missing marker, and `createChart` — the entry
point all five bindings use — never runs `getDataErrors`, so nothing caught
it. The chart rendered one tick with every point stacked on it and no error.

Guard with `typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value)` instead,
which excludes null, undefined, NaN and both infinities in one test. Apply
the equivalent `Number.isFinite(numericValue(value))` check in
`getCategoryDomainForValues`, where it extends the existing Invalid Date
handling to infinities and null.

Fixed at the two domain helpers rather than at the
`getSeriesValuesForProperty` read boundary the finding offers as an
alternative. That boundary would resolve DATA-1 and DATA-2 in one edit, but
the same values also feed tooltips, value labels and `missingValues`
handling, so coercing there changes considerably more than the domain maths.
DATA-2 is fixed separately at its own three stacking sites.

commits.subject: Stop one non-finite value wiping out later series in a stack

original.subject: Fix DATA-2: one non-finite value wipes out the later series in a stack
original.body:
The three stacking accumulators treated only `undefined` as missing. `NaN >= 0`
is false, so a NaN fell into the *negative* branch and was added into
`negativeStackValues[i]`, poisoning the running total for every subsequent
series in that stack at that category. With three stacked series and rows
[{a:5,b:NaN,c:-2},{a:1,b:2,c:-4}], series c's perfectly valid -2 came out NaN,
rendered nothing, and dropped out of the axis domain — with no error anywhere.
Same defect in `getStackPriorValues` and `incrementStackValues`.

Gate all three on one `isStackableValue()` type guard so a non-finite value
takes exactly the path `undefined` already took: emit `undefined` for the
slot, carry the positive accumulator into `prior`, and skip the increment.
Routing it through the existing missing-value path rather than inventing a
third behaviour is what makes the outcome predictable — the regression test
asserts that a NaN row is byte-identical to the same row with the property
simply absent.

Two notes where the finding's detail was off. Its example says the axis domain
"loses the real minimum of -6"; for those rows the real minimum is -4, and the
actual damage is c's -2 going NaN. And Infinity never poisoned the negative
accumulator at all — `Infinity >= 0` sends it down the positive branch, so it
corrupted the axis domain instead, which DATA-1's fix already covers. Both are
kept as tests.

commits.subject: Animate when the axis domain is inverted

original.subject: Fix ANIM-2 (part): an inverted axis domain silently skipped all animation
original.body:
`getSeriesValuesDeltas` weights a value change as
`maxAbsoluteDelta / valueAxisExtent`, gated on `valueAxisExtent > 0`, and
`createValueDeltaData` fed it raw `getDomainExtents`. An explicit axis `min`
above the data (or `max` below it) inverts the domain, making that extent
negative, so every value delta weighted to 0 and the update was applied
instantly — whatever duration was configured, with no warning.
`valueAxes: [{min: 100}]` with data going 10 -> 20 simply snapped.

`createValueDeltaData` now uses a new `getSafeDomainExtents`, and
`getSafeDomainExtent` takes `Math.abs` of a non-collapsed span, which is what
its own comment ("so delta weights stay positive") already claimed. The two
existing series-domain callers are unaffected: `getDomainForValues` never
returns an inverted domain, so only an explicit axis bound can produce one.

Note the finding's collapsed-domain half does not reproduce as written. On a
bar series `[{a:7},{b:7}]` gives the axis domain [0, 7], not [7, 7], because a
value axis defaults its `base` to 0 — the extent is never 0 there. Those cases
are kept as tests and pass either way.

The visual flash the finding leads with is deliberately not addressed here: it
needs a zero-extent domain widened before it reaches the scale, which changes
where an all-equal chart draws when nothing is animating and churns the golden
snapshots. Recorded as a question in REVIEW-FINDINGS-NEW.md.

commits.subject: Open and close the tooltip on pointer enter and leave

original.subject: Fix COMP-1: pointer enter/leave toggled the tooltip instead of opening/closing it
original.body:
With `tooltip.followPointer`, both the enter and the leave handler called
`toggleTooltip`, which flips `tooltipVisible` rather than setting it. Any
other path that changed that flag inverted the pairing for the rest of the
session:

  mouseenter opens -> click the tooltip (closeOnClick) closes it ->
  mouseleave RE-OPENS it, pinned at left:-8px; top:-8px with the pointer
  no longer on the page

  keyboard Enter opens -> mouseenter CLOSES it -> mouseleave re-opens

Replace `toggleTooltip` with `setTooltipOpen(open, payload)` and
`toggleTooltipAtCategory` with `setTooltipOpenAtCategory(open, categoryIndex)`
so every call site states its intent: enter true, leave false, Escape false,
arrow-key open true. Only `onChartClick` and keyboard Enter/Space pass
`!tooltipVisible` — those two are the real toggles.

The body is otherwise untouched. The old `tooltipVisible ? null : x`
expressions ran before the flip and so already read as "what it will be after
this call", making `open ? x : null` exactly equivalent.

commits.subject: Fire onSeriesLayoutBoundsChange after props commit, not from derive

original.subject: Fix COMP-2: onSeriesLayoutBoundsChange fired from inside derive(), before props commit
original.body:
`applyLayoutInfo` invoked the host callback while `Renderer.update()` was
still in `derive` — `this.props` is not assigned until afterwards. Two
consequences:

  1. Stale callback identity. The closure invoked was the *previous*
     render's. Mount with cbA, then update({width, height,
     onSeriesLayoutBoundsChange: cbB}) and cbA ran, not cbB — so hosts that
     pass a fresh closure per render (React, Svelte, Vue) got one closed over
     stale state.

  2. Reentrant update silently discarded. A host that resizes in response to
     the new bounds re-entered update(); the nested update committed fully,
     then the outer update overwrote props/state with the older values. Outer
     400x300 -> callback asks for 500x500 -> the chart ended up 400x300. The
     host's most recent instruction was lost with no error.

Record the bounds in `pendingSeriesLayoutBounds` and flush them from
`measure()`, the component's existing post-commit hook, which reads committed
props. `Renderer.setState` queues measure exactly as `update` does, so the two
setState-driven `applyLayoutInfo` call sites flush on the same path, and mount
is covered by its own `measure(null, null)`.

Same class as the already-fixed ChartController "notify after commit" and the
truncating components' post-setState field writes.

commits.subject: Keep pointer payloads correct when the chart is CSS-scaled

original.subject: Fix COMP-11 (part): pointer payloads broke when the chart was CSS-scaled
original.body:
Pointer coordinates were `clientX - plotRect.left` — CSS pixels, straight from
`getBoundingClientRect()` — and were then divided by the *logical* plot
extents from `seriesLayoutInfo` to derive `categoryPercentage`,
`valuePercentage` and the nearest category. Any CSS scaling of the chart
(`transform: scale()`, a `width: 100%` SVG, page zoom) therefore produced
fractions outside 0-1 and selected the wrong category. The in-bounds test had
the same mismatch.

Add `toPlotLocalPoint(clientX, clientY)`, which divides out the rect's own
scale factor before returning plot-local SVG user units and tests bounds
against the logical extents. Both call sites use it: `processChartEvent` and
`onSeriesShapeClick`, which repeated the same raw subtraction for its
nearest-category lookup. Both cartesian and pie charts route `shapeRef` to
`SeriesBackground`, whose rect is drawn directly from `seriesLayoutInfo`, so
the factor is correct for both chart types.

The coordinate-*frame* half of the finding is deliberately not fixed here.
`chartX`/`chartY` are documented as container-relative and are plot-relative,
but adding the plot offset would silently change the numbers every existing
host receives, and `categoryPosition`/`valuePosition` in the same payload are
documented as plot pixels — so today all four fields share one origin.
Recorded as a question in REVIEW-FINDINGS-NEW.md.

commits.subject: Accept volume-pane fractions at their documented range ends

original.subject: Fix HELP-1: volume-pane fractions at their documented range ends emit an invalid config

  {heightFraction: 0}                     -> maxMarginFraction null    -> blank

commits.subject: Reject duplicate labels in the chart-shape helpers

original.subject: Fix HELP-2: duplicate labels in waterfall/candlestick/OHLC/histogram blank the chart
original.body:
All three helpers wrote `label` straight into the ordinal category column with
no uniqueness check. `getDataErrors` rejects duplicate category values and
`DefaultChartInput.validateDataProvider` swaps in the empty error provider on
any data error, so the whole chart went blank with no message:

  createWaterfall([{label:'Start',total:true,value:100},
                   {label:'Other',value:20},{label:'Other',value:-30}])
  -> getDataErrors: ["category values must be unique, duplicates: Other"]

Two same-named waterfall steps (Other, Adjustments, FX) is ordinary input.
`createHistogram` had the same hole through a custom `binLabel`, which can
collapse distinct bins onto one category value.

`computeWaterfallSteps`, `computeCandlesticks` (so `createOhlc` inherits it)
and over `createHistogram`'s generated labels. `createHeatmap` already threw

commits.subject: Reject NaN and missing OHLC fields in computeCandlesticks

original.subject: Fix HELP-3: computeCandlesticks accepted NaN and missing OHLC fields silently
original.body:
open/high/low/close were copied through unchecked and the direction came from
`close < open`, so bad input produced three different failures, none of them
visible to the caller:

  {open:2, high:NaN, low:1.5, close:1.8} -> downHigh NaN -> a data error, and
    the error provider replaces the whole dataset: one bad tick blanks a
    200-candle chart
  {open:3, low:2, close:3.5}             -> validates, renders a candle with
    no wick that reads as real flat data
  {open:5, high:6, low:4, close:NaN}     -> NaN < 5 is false, so a GREEN
    candle with change: NaN

Throw from a per-candle `checkCandleValues` inside `computeCandlesticks`,
naming the label and the offending key; `createOhlc` inherits it. Also reject
`high < low`, which otherwise renders an upside-down wick. A flat candle where
all four values are equal stays legal.

The finding's alternative — emit undefined for every column so `missingValues`
skips the slot — was rejected because two of the three symptoms are wrong
output rather than missing output. A green down-candle and a wickless candle
both look like real data, so there is nothing for a caller to notice.

commits.subject: Accept the full range of CSS and SVG colours in config

original.subject: Fix CONFIG-1: the color validator rejected most valid CSS/SVG colors
original.body:
The color predicate was a three-regex whitelist — #rgb, #rrggbb, rgb(a,b,c),
rgba(a,b,c,d) — while its message said "should be a valid svg color", which
`red` demonstrably is. In strict mode (the default) any other form invalidated
the whole config, so the chart rendered its config-error state:

  FAIL "red"          FAIL "hsl(200,50%,50%)"   FAIL "transparent"
  FAIL "#ff000080"    FAIL "oklch(0.7 0.1 200)" FAIL "rgb(255 0 0)"
  FAIL "rgb(100%,0%,0%)"

Override `color` in `configValidators` (Object.assign already shadows
movalid's, so one line reaches all eleven call sites), and split it into the
two contracts the fields actually have:

  - Colors mochart interpolates itself — colorScale.min/max/missing/base.* and
    colorPalette entries — delegate to d3-color's parse. That IS the contract:
    what d3 parses is what SeriesColors can interpolate. currentColor and
    var() still fail, preserving the invariant that a keyword must never reach
    a d3 color ramp and interpolate to NaN.

  - Colors written straight to the DOM — shapeStyle/backgroundStyle members,
    gradient stops, tooltip colors — also accept CSS color functions d3-color
    predates. Delegating to d3 alone was not enough here: rgb(255 0 0),
    hsl(200 50% 50%) and oklch() all fail d3's parser but render fine, because
    the browser resolves the attribute, not us.

Document both tiers in guide/config-model.md; the accepted formats were stated
nowhere. movalid is untouched — its zero-dependency status makes the fix there
a separate call, recorded as a question under VAL-1.

The validators.test.ts case asserting `red` is invalid is updated: it was

commits.subject: Apply valueAxisDefaults when no valueAxes entry is declared

original.subject: Fix CONFIG-2: valueAxisDefaults was ignored when no valueAxes entry was declared
original.body:
`valueAxes` is the one list section with an implicit entry
(`singleDefaultIfEmpty`). When the user declared no `valueAxes`,
`applyDefaults` installed the default list verbatim through `copyDefaultsList`
and never merged `allSection` into it, so `valueAxisDefaults` was a complete
no-op — no error, no warning:

  enhanceConfig({ …, valueAxisDefaults: { visible: false, title: 'T' } })
    -> valueAxes: [{ id:'VA0', visible: true,  title: null }]   ignored
  add valueAxes: [{}]
    -> valueAxes: [{ id:'VA0', visible: false, title: 'T'  }]   honoured

`applyAllConfig` could not rescue it either: it merges the all-config *under*
the already-defaulted entry, so every key was shadowed.

Pass `allSection` into `copyDefaultsList` and deep-merge it over each entry.
That covers all three paths that install the defaults list — section
undefined, section present but every entry ignored, and a non-object section —
rather than only the first, so `valueAxes: [{ignore: true}]` behaves like
`valueAxes` absent, which is what "treat it as though it were not specified"
already promises. The other five list sections are unaffected: their defaults
list is empty when nothing is declared, so the merge has nothing to map over.

The library was already tripping over this: helper/sparkline.ts carried
`valueAxes: config.valueAxes ?? [{}]` with the comment "*Defaults sections
only reach declared entries, so declare the default axis". Both are gone.

assertion could not see this class of bug at all. Assert against a
natively-focusable selector list instead. Note `:not([tabindex="-1"])` has to

never the fault line.

domain stays ascending and the animation pipeline is untouched; and clip
rather than drop, with care for markers and labels, which legitimately

original.subject: Write the clipping and clip-indicator design into ANIM-1 part 3
original.body:
Records the design settled in discussion:

- clip rather than drop, partial marks keep their visible portion, and no way
  to switch clipping off;
- clipping is a viewport operation — tooltip, value label and aria still
  report the true value, which is the most valuable part and wants a test;
- the visual is a band on any plot edge where at least one axis clipped, so
  two axes clipping the same end give one band and plot.inverted just remaps
  which edge is "high";
- config on `plot`, not the axes. It renders in the plot area, and per-axis
  config has no answer for two value axes clipping at the same end. Gridlines
  are per-axis plot chrome only because each axis's gridlines sit at different
  positions; a band is one piece of geometry per edge. A new top-level section
  was rejected as too costly for four properties;
- six `plot.clipIndicator*` properties, with AUTO sizing reusing the validator
  and pattern axis.titleSize/tickLabelSize already use;
- it overlays rather than reserving space, keeping it out of the layout
  convergence loop where the tick-truncation reentrancy bug lived, and keeping
  clipIndicatorFront meaningful;
- one label for all edges, hidden rather than truncated when it does not fit,
  rotation matching AxisTitle, and a default string rather than null;
- an SVG <title> rendered always, serving as both the hover tooltip and the
  accessible name — noting it is the first <title> in src, where everything
  else uses ariaLabel, so it needs a comment explaining the divergence.

Closes the parked console.warn sub-question: a visible, hoverable,
screen-reader-named indicator makes clipped data non-silent.

No code changes.

original.subject: Record clip scope for ANIM-1 part 3: clip everything, derived allowance
original.body:
Decision: the clip covers the whole series group — shapes, markers, labels,
error bars — with the rect inflated by the largest markerSize in the chart.

The allowance is needed because margins are only applied to an end whose bound
is AUTO, so on an explicitly-bounded axis (exactly where clipping applies)
data at the bound sits exactly on the plot edge. Measured on a 255px plot, a
markerSize 10 circle at the axis max spans -5.6..5.6 and at the min spans
249.4..260.6, so a plain clip would halve edge markers in charts where nothing
is out of range — a line pinned to min: 0 with a zero value being the everyday
case.

minMarginFraction was considered as the allowance and rejected: it is inert on
explicit bounds (verified: {min:0,max:10} with marginFraction 0.1 leaves the
domain [0,10] while the same margin on an auto end gives [0,11]), and more
fundamentally a margin changes the domain while an allowance does not, so one
property serving both would move the user's data in some configurations and
not others.

Two implementation details left open rather than guessed: one inflated clip
versus two (exact for shapes, inflated for marks), and how label extent
factors in given it needs text measurement.

Also corrects the earlier "markers/labels legitimately overhang" note, which
was my inference from a click-handling comment recorded as though it were a
settled point, and notes that unclipped marks are confined by the svg viewport
rather than escaping onto the page.

original.body:
Found while implementing ANIM-1 part 3. `transformValues` rewrites every
series `property` as `value * 0.6 + 7 + rowIndex`, but for the range-based

right: that data really is outside the pinned axis. But the state is one the
app cannot produce — the real config does not clip, and the demo's own
randomize path re-runs createHeatmap, which recomputes min/max from the row
count. The deeper cost is that four chart types' updated and animated
snapshots pin unreachable states.

Recommended fix uses machinery that already exists: demos.json declares a
`generator` for exactly these types and generateDemoDataProvider re-runs the
core helper, which is what the demo itself does.

original.subject: ANIM-6: cap the animation weight so a clipped value cannot stretch the duration

multiplies the configured duration. It was uncapped, so a value ending far
